page: OVHcloud b3-32 is a general-purpose server instance powered by an AMD EPYC processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 200 GB NVMe SSD, and network connectivity is established with a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps. The virtualization layer is managed through KVM, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25% tier. Multi-core performance, as measured by stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core tests, falls within the middle 50% average. Memory subsystems demonstrate strong write speeds for large uncached blocks and a strong PassMark memory score, though read-only memory bandwidth remains average. Text processing and text generation for small language models with 135M parameters also register in the top 25% performance bracket, while larger model inference and standard database operations align with average baseline expectations.

The absence of hyperthreading ensures dedicated compute resources per vCPU, reducing noisy-neighbor performance degradation. However, this architectural choice limits parallel thread density compared to hyperthreaded alternatives. The qualitative cost efficiency of this instance is supported by its balanced resource density and dedicated CPU allocation, making it suitable for workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, text processing, and moderate database operations that require consistent single-core execution and fast local NVMe storage.
